title: fix(pm-tooling): derive dispatch gates from CI's own path triggers
body:
Fixes #9171

`dispatch-gates.mjs` matched a check family only through the path literals scanned out of the gate's own source. CI decides whether a job runs from a different fact entirely — the workflow's `on.pull_request.paths` list — and nothing reconciled the two. Every dispatch brief tells a dev to derive the gate union with this script and run it, so where the derivation is silent and CI is not, following the instruction exactly still under-runs.

## The trigger, read off the workflow — not inferred, and the card's attribution was wrong

The card observed CI running `Spec property liveness` on a PR whose commit touched `packages/objectql/**`, and both the card and triage flagged that as one hit rather than the rule. Read off `.github/workflows/spec-liveness-check.yml`, the declared trigger is:

```yaml
    paths:
      - 'packages/spec/**'
      - 'packages/qa/dogfood/**'
      - 'content/docs/**'
      - 'docs/audits/**'
```

`packages/objectql/**` is **not** in it. PR #9166's full file list contains `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`, `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` and `content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx` — GitHub's `paths` filter applies to the whole PR diff, not the commit the card cited, so `content/docs/**` is what scheduled the job. Inferring `packages/objectql/**` would have installed a rule CI does not have, in the exact mirror that drifted.

The card's real premise holds and is worse than stated: the derivation named `check:liveness` for **no path at all**, `packages/spec/**` included — the job's own first trigger.

## The measurement the card asked for

Every workflow's declared `pull_request` trigger, diffed against what the derivation named for a probe path inside each declared glob. 25 workflow files, 103 discovered families.

**Six** workflows declare a `paths:` filter. Four of them contribute check families:

| workflow | declared globs | families | (trigger, family) pairs CI schedules that the derivation named in NEITHER half |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec-liveness-check.yml` | 4 | 4 | **16** — every glob × every family |
| `validate-deps.yml` | 9 | 3 | **23** |
| `prerelease-pin-watch.yml` | 3 | 1 | **2** |
| `engine-split-metric.yml` | 2 | 1 | **1** |
| `docs-drift-check.yml` | 3 | 0 | — (see the finding below) |
| `scaffold-e2e.yml` | 3 | 0 | — |
| **total** | | | **42** |

After this change the same harness reports **0**. The remaining 19 workflows declare no `paths:` filter at all: CI schedules those on every PR, so they carry no path signal to reconcile — that count is now printed in the residue instead of being an absence nobody could size (94 of 103 on this tree).

All four gates of the liveness job scored `undetermined` — they read the metadata-type registry rather than a path, so they carry no watch hint and never could. No improvement to the hint scan reaches them; only CI's own declaration does.

## Option 1 or option 2 — priced, and why this is both

A hand-written map from `packages/spec/**` to `check:liveness` is the one implementation this file's contract forbids: "this script embeds NO list of checks and NO map from paths to checks". It would be a second copy of a fact the workflow already states — the same declared-vs-enforced drift the card names, one level down. So option 1 done correctly **is** reading the trigger, which is option 2's "derive from the workflow's own job triggers".

Priced honestly: the parse is one indentation walk over text the run already reads, alongside the `runCommandTexts` walk that established the idiom. It came to one file, `+449 -40`, most of that the docblocks this file's convention requires plus 36 new self-test cases — cheap while already in there, so it was taken.

Option 2's other half — "diff against, so a job CI schedules and the script omits is itself a failure" — is **subsumed, not skipped**. Deriving *from* the trigger makes omission structurally impossible for a paths-filtered workflow; there is no residual state for a diff to catch. For an unfiltered workflow CI schedules everything, so the same guard would be trivially unsatisfiable. Nothing is half-built and no follow-up card is owed for it.

## What changed

- `extractTriggerPaths` — `on.pull_request.paths` in declaration order, block and flow sequences, decoy lists outside the `on:` mapping excluded, `pull_request_target` not mistaken for `pull_request`.
- `triggerPatternRegex` / `triggerCovers` / `triggerListCovers` — GitHub's filter-pattern language rather than an approximation of it: `**` crosses `/`, `*` does not, `?` `+` `[]` keep their documented meaning, and `!` negations are evaluated **in order**, both directions. The directory-surface reach is decided on the pattern's literal prefix, which refuses the reach a leading `**` would claim (`**/package.json` never claims an arbitrary directory) — the same trade `hintCovers` records, decided the same way.
- `coveringHint` becomes `coveringKey` and returns provenance. Precedence is identity, then CI trigger, then scanned literal: a declaration outranks this tool's inference, and the `matched via` column now says which, so a lead can never be read as the wrong kind of claim.
- The residue sizes the unfiltered-workflow families and refuses to render that count as `undefined`.

Boundary stated in the source with the direction it fails in: `paths-ignore:` is not modelled — no workflow in this tree uses it, and one that did would parse as "no filter" and fall back to today's behaviour, a possible missing lead and never a fabricated one. `merge_group` supports no `paths` and only ever widens what CI runs, so ignoring it cannot make the derivation over-claim.

## Verification

Union run at final commit `4cc72114f`:

- `node scripts/pm/check-dispatch-gates.mjs` (the derived family for this path) — `219 cases pass`, exit 0. The baseline at the branch point passes 183, so 36 of them are new.
- `node scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs` — OK, 6023 text files, exit 0. Plus a self-scan of the changed file for control bytes: clean.
- Gate list re-derived against the actual changed path with the fixed script: `check:pm-dispatch-gates` only, matching the dispatch brief with nothing added.

Live specimen, end to end — PR #9166's real file surface now derives what CI ran on it:

```
$ node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx \
      packages/objectql/src/declared-fields.ts pnpm-lock.yaml
  - pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:liveness   [spec-liveness-check.yml]
        matched via content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx ⇢ CI trigger in spec-liveness-check.yml 'content/docs/**'
  ... + check:empty-state, check:variant-docs, check:strictness-ledger (same job)
  ... + check:override-consistency, check-changeset-fixed, check-osv-exemptions via 'pnpm-lock.yaml'
```

Reverse verification, direction predicted before running (ordinary red) and observed as predicted: with `coveringTrigger` ablated to return null on the committed tree, **6 of 219** cases fail — the trigger cases and all three live `spec-liveness-check.yml` pins — while `identity still outranks CI trigger` and `an entry with no triggers at all behaves exactly as before` stay green, which is what makes the ablation targeted rather than blunt. Restored by `git checkout` from the branch; tree byte-identical to `4cc72114f`. One test was rewritten as a result: the provenance assertion indexed straight into `hits[0]` and *threw* under ablation, aborting the run before the live pins reported — it now reads defensively so a regression fails the case and the gate still says what else it checked.

## Scope

No changeset: `scripts/pm/**` is internal dispatch tooling and publishes nothing. `skip-changeset` applied.

One out-of-scope finding, filed rather than repaired in this PR — **#9187** — `extractCheckInvocations` discovers a family only from `pnpm check:NAME` or a `node scripts/.../check-NAME.mjs` filename, so `docs-drift-check.yml`'s `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --self-test` step is discovered as nothing at all. It is the one paths-filtered workflow this PR's trigger key still buys nothing for, because it has no discovered family to attach a trigger to. Different fix surface (discovery, not matching).

#9144 remains open and is untouched here — same blind-spot class on the `check:i18n` edge, deliberately kept separate. The measurement above did not reach it: `check:i18n` runs in `lint.yml`, which declares no `paths:` filter, so the trigger key cannot see it and its `CHANGE_KIND_GATES` entry is still the only thing that names it.
